Subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up — Paywise / Redwood

Hi Emily / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed around encryption and key management so everyone is aligned: 

TL;DR: Redwood supports TLS 1.2+ for in-transit encryption, AES-256 at-rest encryption, and we offer both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integrations). For Paywise's regulated workload you indicated preference for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) with automated key rotation and audit logging.

Recap of what we covered:
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS available for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption across object stores and attached volumes.
- Customer-managed keys: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM-backed workflows for Private deployments.
- Key rotation & separation: Redwood can support automated rotation or allow Paywise to rotate keys from your KMS; we do not hold plaintext keys.
- Audit & logging: Key usage logs (KMS calls) are available in our audit logs; we can export to your SIEM and provide per-request tracing at the token/request-id level.

Open items / actions we agreed:
1) Paywise to send the detailed KMS/crypto requirements doc (scope, rotation cadence, HSM requirement).
2) Redwood to provide a short FAQ on CMK (customer-managed keys) behavior for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
3) Technical deep-dive session (30–45m) with Dev/Infra teams to validate HSM connectivity and network routes — proposed next week.
4) Provide sample audit logs and a redacted KMS usage runbook for compliance review.

Attachments: I’ll attach a short FAQ and a sample audit-log export for your review (see next message).

Proposed next step: Emily, can you confirm your preferred time for the technical deep-dive? Also please attach the KMS requirements doc when you have a moment.

Best,
Marissa

Emily —

Appreciate the doc. Quick answers to your Qs below, and next steps.

1) Hosted (Redwood-managed): We never export customer CMKs out of the cloud KMS. For Hosted we offer two patterns: (a) Redwood-managed keys (we manage the key lifecycle) and (b) CMK where Paywise grants Redwood a binding role to use keys in your KMS; Redwood does not obtain plaintext keys in either case. For regulated HSM-backed credentials we recommend Dedicated or Private.

2) Dedicated: mTLS is available and we can require mutual TLS for all inter-node and API traffic for Dedicated clusters. For Hosted (public API) mTLS is opt-in and would require SAML+network allowlisting — we can discuss trade-offs in the deep-dive.

3) KMS audit logs: We can include per-request metadata: request-id, model-request-id, and object id mappings in the audit export. We will provide a sample redacted log as requested.

Attachments: redwood_kms_faq.pdf (short FAQ) and sample-audit-log-redacted.txt (inline sample) — see attached.

Proposed next steps (to keep momentum):
- Schedule deep-dive (Dev/Infra) — we can do Thu 12/3 10am PT.
- I’ll share a short SOW snippet for HSM connectivity requirements for Dedicated/Private.
- Redwood to provide sample logs and a one-page runbook for your auditors.

Emily — if Thu 10am PT works I’ll send an invite with Zoom + an agenda.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood_kms_faq.pdf; sample-audit-log-redacted.txt
